TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: June 26, 2025 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of the Certain Documents Relative to the Development, Construction, and Financing of New University Housing Purpose of Submittal: To recommend the Board of Trustees Finance and Facilities Committee recommend approval to the Board of Trustees of the New University Housing (NUH) Project and authorize execution of documents for the development, construction, and financing of two new on- campus undergraduate student housing communities and one graduate student and family housing community at the University of Rhode Island.
Background: In late 2022, the University of Rhode Island engaged a planning team led by Scion Advisory Services, with architects from CannonDesign, to develop a Housing and Residential Life Housing Master Plan to transform URI housing.

This initiative align ed with URI’s strategic commitment to enhanc e the student experience by providing modern, affordable, and desirable living spaces.
The plan recommended that URI pursue a public-private-partnership (P3) to address immediate housing needs on the Kingston campus.
In May 2024, URI issued a public request for proposal for a development partner, and after a thorough vetting process, selected Gilbane Development Company (Gilbane) as its P3 partner.
In September 2024, the University entered into a Preliminary Development Agreement (PDA) with Gilbane.
In March 2025, the University approved the feasibility study conducted by Gilbane confirming that the project was feasible and would move forward.
Gilbane then selected, with URI’s concurrence, Provident to serve as the project 501(c)(3) partner.
PRG – RI Properties LLC, a single member limited liability company, was organized by Provident for the Project.
URI DevCo LLC, a single purpose subsidiary of Gilbane, was also organized for development of the Project.

In April 2025, URI DevCo, Provident, and Raymond James (underwriter) commenced the application process to issue debt through the Rhode Island Health and Education Building Corporation (RIHEBC).
The Project is summarized below.
Project Overview: Project Scope & Design: • Total Beds: 1,134 • Planned Housing Phases: o Occupancy in Fall 2027: 514 undergraduate beds o Occupancy in Fall 2028: 400 undergraduate beds o Occupancy in Fall 2028: 220 graduate beds

• Building Types: o Undergraduate Housing (Two Buildings): Apartment-style, single bedrooms in two- and four- bedroom units.
Modular construction. o Graduate Housing (Six Buildings + Community Center): Apartments with studio, one-bedroom, two-bedroom, and three-bedroom configurations.
Modular rebuild on existing foundations. o All buildings meet state code and URI design standards.
Financial Summary (rounded): • Total Project Cost: $231MM (as of June 2025). • URI Equity Contribution: The University may fund an equity contribution to the Project, the amount of which is currently subject to negotiation, and will be up to the amount authorized by the Board during executive session. • Rental Rates: Rental rates are within acceptable range to URI Housing and Residential Life, though may need to increase due to changes in market conditions. • Annual Rate Escalation: 3% • Expected Occupancy Rate: 95% • Debt Term: 40 years (all-in). • Debt Coverage Ratio: 1.2x or better (Senior Debt). • Residual Cash Flow to URI: $317MM over the term (NPV @ 5% = $63.7MM).

Document Approval Over the past several months, the University has negotiated and vetted several Project documents, three of which are being brought to the Board today for approval, and two of which are being shared for informational purposes.

These documents, listed below, are described in more detail in the enclosed Board of Trustees resolutions. • The Ground Lease between the University and the Provident , will extend for a term of up to 42 years and will contain provisions requiring the Project to be constructed in accordance with campus standards (for approval). • The Affiliation Agreement between the University and Provident , which outlines each entity’s obligations to the project (for approval). • The Interim Management Agreement between the University and URI DevCo LLC, which will allow the University to continue to manage the graduate student housing until the expected turnover date of May 2026, at which time it will be turned over to the Developer for demolition and re -construction (for approval). • The Turnkey Development Agreement between URI DevCo LLC and Provident, pursuant to which the Developer will implement the design, construction, and commissioning of the Project for a stipulated sum in accordance with plans approved by the University (for information). • The Project Management Agreement between Provident and Inwood Management, outlining operations and maintenance of the Student Housing Facilities (for information).

Next Steps Upon the Board’s approval of the Project and authorization to continue negotiating required documents, URI will finalize the negotiation and execute the relevant documents.
The Project is scheduled for financial close in September 2025, at which point the final Project budget will be determined.
We look forward to continued collaboration with Gilbane to ensure this critical project’s seamless and successful implementation.
Supporting Information: The following documents are enclosed: • Board of Trustees Resolutions • DRAFT Ground Lease • DRAFT Affiliation Agreement

• DRAFT Interim Management Agreement • DRAFT Turnkey Development Agreement • DRAFT Project Management Agreement • Schematic outlining the structure of the P3 Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the Board of Trustees Approve the Project and authorize each Authorized Officer to Execute Development, Construction, and Financing of the two (2) new on-campus undergraduate student housing communities and one (1) on-campus graduate student and family housing community at the University of Rhode Island and to execute documents and take actions, all as further described in the enclosed resolutions.

4900-8991-3674.4 BOARD MEETING June 27, 2025 RESOLUTIONS APPROVE PROJECT AND AUTHORIZE EXECUTION OF DOCUMENTS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT, CONSTRUCTION, AND FINANCING OF TWO (2) NEW ON -CAMPUS UNDERGRADUATE STUDENT HOUSING COMMUNITIES AND ONE (1) ON -CAMPUS GRADUATE STUDENT AND FAMILY HOUSING COMMUNITY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND Action: Approve the Project and authorize each Authorized Officer to Execute Development, Construction, and Financing of the two (2) new on -campus undergraduate student housing communities and one (1) on -campus graduate student and family housing community at the University of Rhode Island and to execute documents and take actions , all as further described in the following resolutions On September 27, 2024, the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees (the “ Board”) approved entering into a public -private partnership pre liminary development agreement with Gilbane Development Company in order to design and construct two (2) new on -campus undergraduate student housing communities and one (1) on -campus graduate student and family housing community as further describe below (collectively, the “ Project”) at the University of Rhode Island (the “ University”) and any authorized signatories (as defined in the Policy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents) to negotiate the terms of any documents relating to the Project .

The Project consists of the development, construction, furnishing, and equipping of the Student Housing Facilities (as defined below).
Accordingly, it is recommended that, subject to resolution of final contract and development terms to the satisfaction of an Authorized Officer, the Board approve and delegate to each of the Chair of the Board of Trustees, the President and the Vice President of Administration and Finance ( together, the “Authorized Officers”) the authority to execute all necessary or appropriate documents, including the Ground Lease Agreement, the Affiliation Agreement, and the Interim Management Agreement, in substantially the form enclosed herewith, subject to such changes as any Authorized Officer executing any such document may approve, and that the Authorized Officers and any other authorized signatories (as defined in the Policy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents) are each authorized to execute any other related agreements, certificates or documents, and take any other actions necessary or appropriate for the development, construction, and financing of the Project.

An Authorized Officer’s execution of the Ground Lease Agreement, the Affiliation Agreement, or the Interim Management Agreement, shall be conclusive evidence of its approval by the Board and University.

2 4900-8991-3674.4 Undergraduate and Graduate Student Housing URI DEVCO LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability company (“ Developer”), has been engaged to perform the development, construction, furnishing, and equipping of the two (2) new on-campus undergraduate student housing communities: (i) an approximately 135,177 gross square foot apartment-style building with approximately 400 student beds (“ Student Housing Facility 1 ”) located on the portion of the Kingston campus; and (ii) an approximately 173,739 gross square foot apartment-style building with approximately 514 student beds (“ Student Housing Facility 2” and, together with Student Housing Facility 1, the “ Undergraduate Student Housing Facilities”) located on a portion of the Kingston campus.

In addition to Student Housing Facility 1 and Student Housing Facility 2, Developer has been engaged to complete the demolition, design, development, construction, furnishing, and equipping of one (1) on -campus graduate student and family housing community comprised of a mix of studio, one -bed, two -bed and three -bed apartment style units with a total of approximately 22 0 student beds (“Student Housing Facility 3” or “ Graduate Student Housing Facility ”) located on a portion of the Kingston campus.
Student Ho using Facility 1, Student Housing Facility 2, and Student Housing Facility 3 shall hereinafter be collectively referred to as the “Student Housing Facilities.” The Board recognizes that the existing student housing facilities for undergraduate and graduate students at the University are insufficient.
For the Project to proceed, it is necessary to delegate authority to the Authorized Officer to execute the development, construction, and financing documents.
Accordingly, the President of the University and Vice President of Administration and Finance of the University, with the concurrence of the appropriate administrative officers, recommends that the foregoing be approved.

Public-Private Partnership Project Summary and Scope The Project is structured as a concession agreement with a private qualified development firm to enter into a public -private partnership (“ P3”), which requires a ground lease for the structure and the issuance of bonds by the Rhode Island Health and Educational Building Corporation (the “ Issuer”).
This P3 is a delivery approach , whereby, w hen appropriate and feasible, the University can utilize the P3 model to secure the anticipated advantages of increased speed of delivery, guaranteed maximum price and fi rm delivery date, and sharing risk with the private sector.
In a P3 model, the University leases its land to a tax-exempt nonprofit entity in the form of a ground lease.
That entity engages the developer and contractors to construct the buildings.
The nonprofit entity owns the buildings until the debt is retired.
At that time, ownership reverts to the University, and the ground lease terminates.
Development Process In support of this Project planning, the University solicited proposals on April 30, 2024 for the development and construction of the Student Housing Facilities.

As a result of the solicitation process, Gilbane Development Company, a Rhode Island corporation , was chosen as the lead developer to implement the development financing, construction, equipping, and operation of the

3 4900-8991-3674.4 Project.
URI DevCo LLC, a single purpose subsidiary of Gilbane Development Company , was organized by Gilbane Development Company for development of the Project (the “Developer”).
As a part of the team, Provident Resources Group, Inc ., a nonprofit 501(c)(3) tax -exempt organization established to assist colleges and universities across the country in providing academic and related facilities for their students and otherwise furthering their education missions, (“Provident”) will serve as the tax-exempt parent and sole member of the ground lessee and owner of the facilities , PRG – RI Properties LLC, a single member limited liability company (the “Lessee/Borrower”).
The Lessee/Borrower will be organized exclusively to carry out the Project and is not expected to have any assets other than those that are associated with the Project .
The selected team includes Gilbane Building Company, a Rhode Island corporation, as the general contractor and Raymond James as the underwriter .
The architecture partner is CannonDesign.
Inwood Management will perform operations and maintenance of the Student Housing Facilities.

Following the award to the Developer, the University for itself and on behalf of the Board entered into a pre liminary development agreement with the Developer to conduct pre -development and design activities for the Project as a whole before bond issuance and closing, currently targeted for September 1, 2025, which date may be subject to change.
The entire process that led to the award of this transaction was reviewed and approved by the Rhode Island Division of Purchases through the URI Office of Strategic Procurement.
Project Structure, Financing and Document Package The total cost of the Project is currently estimated to be approximately $231M, which is expected to be financed through the bond issuance by the Issuer.
The proceeds of the bonds will be l oaned by the Issuer to the Lessee/Borrower.
The University may also fund an equity contribution, the amount of which is currently subject to negotiation and will be up to the amount authorized by the Board during executive session.
The proposed financing structure for the Project will be based on a privatized P3 financi ng model through which the Board will ground lease the land on which the Project is located to the Lessee/Borrower.

The Ground Lease for the Project between the University and the Lessee/Borrower (the “Ground Lease”) will extend for a term of up to 42 years, which will be in excess of the maturity of the proposed bond financing, and will contain provisions requiring the Project to be constructed in accordance with campus standards.
Provisions in the Ground Lease and Affiliation Agreement will also include certain areas of support and cooperation between the University and the Lessee/Borrower.
Under the Ground Lease, the land will always remain owned by the University, and the Lessee/Borrower will own the Student Housing Facilities for the term of the financing.
Annual rent to the University will be Net Available Cash Flow from the Project, estimated over the life of the lease to be approximately $317,157,460.
A copy of the form of the Ground Lease, subject to further negotiation and execution as described herein, is attached hereto.

The University and the Lessee/Borrower will also enter into an affiliation agreement (“Affiliation Agreement”) to provide for the University’s obligations with respect to the Project, including the leasing of the Undergraduate Housing Project consistent with its leasing of other on- campus undergraduate student housing.
A copy of the form of the Affiliation Agreement, subject to further negotiation and execution as described herein, is attached hereto.

4 4900-8991-3674.4 The Graduate Student Housing Facility will be turned over to the Developer for demolition and reconstruction after the end of the 2025 -2026 academic year.
During the period between closing and turnover, the University will continue to manage the existing graduate village housing consistent with existing management practices pursuant to an interim management agreement (the “Interim Management Agreement”).
A copy of the form of Interim Management Agreement , subject to further negotiation and execution as described herein, is attached hereto.
The Developer and the Lessee/Borrower will enter into a turnkey development agreement (the “Turnkey Development Agreement”) pursuant to which the Developer will implement the design, construction, and commissioning of the Project for a stipulated sum in accordance with plans approved by the University.
The Turnkey Development Agreement is expected to be in substantially the form attached hereto.

Pursuant to the Management Agreement between Lessee/Borrower and Inwood Management (the “Management Agreement”), Inwood Management will perform operations and maintenance of the Student Housing Facilities , including all leasing and management of the Graduate Student Housing Facility, in accordance with the Responsibility Matrix attached to the Management Agreement.
The Management Agreement is expected to be in substantially the form attached hereto.
P3 Agreement Package The University, for itself and on behalf of the Board of Trustees, is required to enter into a series of agreements with the Lessee/Borrower and Developer to authorize and complete the Project, and to give such approvals and take such other actions and enter into other agreements consistent with the Ground Lease, as the parties consider necessary and appropriate in connection with the development, construction, financing, and operation of the Project as described above .

The principal documents that the Authorized Officer will execute will be the Ground Lease, the Affiliation Agreement and the Interim Management Agreement, each substantially in the form of the listed agreements attached hereto, subject to such further negotiation and changes as any Authorized Officer executing any such document may approve .
URI has also been actively engaged in the review and negotiation of the Turnkey Develo pment Agreement and Property Management Agreement to ensure they align with the University’s overarching goals and desired outcomes of the Project.
